scenes.title: The Goal and Constraints
scenes.narration_text:
Your goal is simple: eliminate all disease.

The constraint is also simple: resources are scarce. You have limited money, time, and talent.
scenes.context: The speaker introduces the core mission of global disease eradication and the reality of resource scarcity.

Your economist Mancur Olson identified why public goods are systematically underproduced: diffuse benefits and concentrated costs.

scenes.title: Concentrated Interest
scenes.narration_text: In simpler terms: everyone benefits from a cure for cancer, but nobody benefits enough to fight for it the way a weapons manufacturer fights for a bomber contract.
scenes.context: Contrasting the fragmented interest in health with the intense, focused interest in military procurement.

scenes.title: The Invisible Problem
scenes.narration_text: It's one of those observations that's obvious once someone says it, and invisible before, which describes most of your species' problems.

scenes.context: Clarifying that the DIH is an additive layer designed to support experimental medicine.

scenes.context: Introducing Sarah, an example patient struggling under the current healthcare system.

scenes.context: Summarizing Sarah's situation: high costs and low medical efficacy due to a lack of options.

scenes.title: Doctor's Trial Search
scenes.narration_text: With your Decentralized Institutes of Health: Her doctor checks the trial network during a regular visit. Sees relevant trials.
scenes.context: A doctor uses a decentralized network to find clinical trials during a patient visit.

scenes.title: One-Click Enrollment
scenes.narration_text: Recommends one based on Sarah's profile. Sarah enrolls with one click. The trial coverage pool covers all costs. Sarah pays a small copay.
scenes.context: Sarah effortlessly joins a clinical trial recommended by her doctor, with costs covered.

scenes.title: Patient Data Reporting
scenes.narration_text: Gets an experimental drug that might work better. Reports blood sugar via app. Her data helps the next patient.
scenes.context: Sarah participates in the trial by taking medicine and logging data to help future patients.

scenes.title: Efficient Consultations
scenes.narration_text:
Total time added to doctor visit: three minutes.

Why your doctors will cooperate:

More treatment options for desperate patients.
scenes.context: The system is efficient and provides doctors with more options for patients in need.

scenes.title: Doctor Benefits
scenes.narration_text:
No liability (covered by trial insurance).

Minimal workflow changes.

Why your patients will use it:
scenes.context: Doctors are incentivized by low liability and simple workflow integrations.

scenes.title: Patient Incentives
scenes.narration_text:
Affordable access to experimental treatments.

Doctor-recommended.

Insurance-like coverage (familiar model).

No financial risk.
scenes.context: Patients benefit from low-cost, low-risk access to treatments recommended by their own doctors.

scenes.title: The Guinea Pig Paradox
scenes.narration_text:
They help others while helping themselves.

It's like being a guinea pig, except the guinea pig gets paid and gets medicine.
scenes.context: Clinical trials become a mutually beneficial arrangement rather than a risky burden.

No C.E.O., no board, no one to corrupt.

scenes.title: Self-Sustaining Ecosystem
scenes.narration_text: Your ecosystem handles most research funding automatically: companies register treatments, patients join trials, revenue flows, research happens.
scenes.context: The primary research engine runs through commercial activity and patient choices.

scenes.title: Targeted DIH Funding
scenes.narration_text: Your Decentralized Institutes of Health only directs the one percent Treaty Fund to cover what the market genuinely can't.
scenes.context: DIH acts as a safety net for research that would otherwise be ignored.

scenes.title: Minimalist Design
scenes.narration_text:
What Your Decentralized Institutes of Health Outsources (and Why).

Your Decentralized Institutes of Health is intentionally minimal.
scenes.context: The organization stays small to maximize impact and prevent organizational bloat.

scenes.title: Avoiding Corruption
scenes.narration_text: It outsources everything operational because the best way to avoid corruption is to have nothing worth corrupting.
scenes.context: By removing operational power from the center, the risk of capture is eliminated.

scenes.title: The Restaurant Model
scenes.narration_text:
If a provider stops performing, you fund a better one. This is how your species runs restaurants.

Time to try it with medicine.
scenes.context: Competition and performance-based funding are applied to medical services.

scenes.title: Outsourced Infrastructure
scenes.narration_text: Trial infrastructure is outsourced to competing providers (funded campaigns) to separate concerns.
scenes.context: Separating the management of trials from the scientific direction to ensure integrity.

scenes.title: Existing Platforms
scenes.narration_text: Crowdfunding is outsourced to existing platforms because they already exist and work.
scenes.context: The DIH leverages current technology rather than building redundant systems.

scenes.title: Talent Marketplaces
scenes.narration_text: Talent matching is outsourced to existing marketplaces to avoid reinventing what already works.
scenes.context: Professionals are matched with research needs using proven market platforms.

scenes.title: Market Competition
scenes.narration_text: Data storage is outsourced to competing providers to encourage market competition.
scenes.context: Outsourcing data ensures competitive pricing and innovation in storage technology.

scenes.title: Campaign Lifecycle
scenes.narration_text: Every outsourced function follows the same lifecycle: propose, vote via Wishocracy, receive funding, deliver, get measured,
scenes.context: Every part of the system is subject to democratic oversight and performance measurement.

scenes.context: The system remains secure through outcome-based funding and decentralization.
